result.summary: The failed transfer to WARD-B/BAY2-04 (event time 09:20Z, MSG02202, HTTP 503 ward_unavailable) was overtaken. The receiver is at version 2, and the transfer applied there was to WARD-C/BAY1-07 (event time 09:45Z, MSG02203, version_after 2). That event happened strictly later, so this matches catalogue E1. Resending would move the patient backwards to WARD-B. Under DEP-2.2 the bed board would then show the wrong bed, pharmacy would send medicines to the wrong ward and porters would get a task for a move that already happened. The version condition would not stop this if the resend were checked against the current v2. Reconciling is wrong because the receipt lookup returned 404, so this transfer was never committed. Doing nothing leaves the receiver correct at WARD-C v2, with nothing changing for consumers. The route supports conditional writes, receipts and dry runs, and the epoch is 107. Only the receiver's record can be checked from here. The effects on consumers are inferred (DEP-1.1).
unknowns: Whether the downstream consumers (bed board, pharmacy, porters, EPR) correctly handled the WARD-A to WARD-C move can't be seen from the integration engine (DEP-1.1).
Whether the site would rather keep a complete movement history (the correct_history alternative). The route's history_policy is 'current', so this seems unlikely.
